column1: # Which MSigDB terms the Metabolic collection is made of.
# One term per line: MSigDB systematic id, tab, category. A line beginning "!"
# is a term that was JUDGED AND LEFT OUT on purpose — it is recorded so that
# derive-metabolic.mjs's staleness check can tell "nobody has looked at this
# yet" from "somebody looked and said no", and so the second is arguable in a
# Every one of the 15,646 term names in the pathway and ontology collections was
# read and judged against written criteria — the union across human and mouse,
# since they share systematic ids, so each term is decided once. It replaced a
# name-matching vocabulary, which is only ever as good as the correlation
# between what a pathway is called and what it is about. That correlation fails
# exactly where it matters: the vocabulary missed KEGG_PENTOSE_AND_
# GLUCURONATE_INTERCONVERSIONS, a metabolic map with no metabolic word in it;
# subject is metabolic control; and KEGG_TYPE_II_DIABETES_MELLITUS. No
# vocabulary catches those without catching half of signalling with them.
# The biochemistry of small molecules — synthesis, breakdown, interconversion —
# energy metabolism, redox and one-carbon, storage and mobilisation, the
# transport of metabolites, the pathways that REGULATE metabolism, metabolic
# disease, metabolic enzyme activities, and the compartments that exist to do
# metabolism. Not: macromolecule turnover, which GO also calls metabolism
# (protein, RNA and DNA metabolic processes, translation, proteasome); the
# top-of-hierarchy terms that cover everything; or signalling and development
# The library said "oxidative phosphorylation" 60 times over, in 60 sets
# that are the same claim at different resolutions — every electron-transfer
# step, every respiratory complex's assembly, each database's own copy. That is
# 60 rows in a results table for one finding and 60 of the tests the
# Benjamini-Hochberg correction is spread across. The family is consolidated to
# four: Hallmark's and KEGG's oxidative phosphorylation, Reactome's aerobic
# respiration, and mitochondrial biogenesis, which is a different question from
# respiring. Terms whose subject is another family that merely happens in the
# mitochondrion — beta-oxidation, the TCA cycle, iron-sulfur clusters,
# mitochondrial fatty acid synthesis — stay with their own kind.
# Ribosomes and translation needed no consolidation: they are macromolecule
# turnover and the criteria never admitted them. The one survivor,
# metabolism and is named for what it is NOT.
# 2813 terms included, 428 recorded as deliberately excluded.
